# Evaluating an agent

The `replaylab-eval` command plays a language model through the same campaign
any scripted policy plays: same pools, same hidden outcomes, same scoring, the
only difference being that batches come from a model reasoning over the tools
you gave it. The whole workflow is one command family (install the extras
first: `uv sync --extra eval`).

## The pieces

**Conditions** are experiment arms defined in `config/conditions.yaml`: an
`include` list (tool groups or tool names) and an optional `exclude`. Every
condition sees the *same* system prompt — only the tool set changes, so a
comparison between conditions measures exactly that difference. Print the
resolved tool list of each one with:

```bash
replaylab-eval conditions
```

**Models and prices** live in `config/models.yaml` and `config/prices.yaml`
(one entry per model key; the API key is read from the environment variable
named in the config, never from the repository). Prices feed the spend guard —
an unpriced model cannot run.

**One records file per experiment.** Every finished episode appends a single
JSON line to `<run-dir>/episodes.jsonl` holding the outcome (`scores`), the
full conversation (`messages`), a per-call audit (`tool_calls`), token usage
and cost, the stop reason, quality `flags`, and the `config_hash`/`git_sha`
that produced it. Episodes that fail (provider error, truncated reply, spend
cap) leave **no line at all** — rerunning the same command plays exactly the
missing ones and skips everything recorded.

## The workflow

```bash
# 1. the pilot: play n episodes, measure cost, project the whole matrix
replaylab-eval pilot --run-dir runs/x --model deepseek \
    --games N-dev --conditions A,B1 --trials 20 --max-usd 1

# 2. the run: play every missing episode of the matrix (resumable)
replaylab-eval run --run-dir runs/x --model deepseek \
    --games N-dev --conditions A,B1 --trials 20 --max-usd 1

# 3. baselines on the same seeds, in the same records file
replaylab-eval scripted --run-dir runs/x --games N-dev \
    --policies random,learner,learner_sim,learner_sim_purchased --trials 20

# 4. paired comparison: a minus b, bootstrap over seeds
replaylab-eval compare --records runs/x/episodes.jsonl \
    --game N-dev --a B1 --b scripted:learner_sim --ci 0.9

# 5. read the whole run as a page
replaylab-eval view --run-dir runs/x
```

Both `pilot` and `run` refuse to start when the projected cost exceeds
`--max-usd`; once running, the cap is checked before **every** model call and
the running total persists in `spend.json`, so a resumed run keeps counting
against the same cap. Caps are cumulative per run directory — when you extend
an experiment, raise the cap to cover what is already spent plus the new
projection.

## Why the comparisons are fair

* **Pairing.** The episode seed depends only on `(game, trial)` — never on
  condition or model — so `B1` and `scripted:learner_sim` face the identical
  pool shuffle and aliases. `compare` refuses to run unless the two sides have
  exactly the same seeds, and reports the mean paired difference, a bootstrap
  interval, and the win/tie/loss ledger (`--trial-range` restricts to a block
  of trials).
* **One configuration per claim.** `config_hash` covers the model, prices,
  prompts, conditions, tool descriptions and limits. Two records with the same
  hash came from the same configuration; the commit is stamped alongside it.
* **Nothing is replayed for luck.** A recorded episode is never deleted or
  re-dealt; a *failed* one is replayed because it never existed as data.

## Reading a run

`compare` prints one JSON object: `mean_diff` (a − b; positive = a better),
`ci_low`/`ci_high`, `wins`/`ties`/`losses`, `n`. Before reading hit counts,
check the run's health the way the reports do: no (or few) failure lines in
`errors.jsonl`, every episode ending `finished` or `agent_stopped`, a single
`config_hash`, all scripted rows present for the trials being judged — and
read a couple of transcripts in the viewer, whose `flags` totals sit next to
every verdict.

The viewer (`replaylab-eval view`) turns the records file into one
self-contained HTML page: the tool timeline of each episode, the hidden pool
under its aliases, and optionally scripted episodes overlaid as ghosts —
scripted plays are deterministic per seed, so the overlay is exact.

Finally, when a campaign ends, the model is asked once more **without tools**
for the plain-text summary the system prompt promises; it appears as the last
message in the viewer. The epilogue is best effort: if the provider fails it,
the finished episode is still recorded (flagged `closing_summary_failed`).

## Before an experiment is believed

Every comparison above is only as good as its discipline: decide the question,
the trials and the pass/fail rule *before* running, run the validity checks
before reading outcomes, and report every comparison that was decided on — not
only the flattering ones. The project's working notes hold the registrations
and results in that order.
